_comment: THE QUERY-PLAN ALLOWLIST (#1135). A read that plans as a full scan of a table over `scanFloorRows` rows, or as a sort of every row it read on a paged read, fails `crates/core/tests/query_plans.rs` unless it is listed here with its home and the one-line reason it is fine. Down-only: `scanFloorRows` may only fall (a lower floor checks more tables) and each `allowed` count may only fall, so the allowlist cannot grow in the change that needs it; an entry no read needs any more fails the test too. The fix for a hot read is the index it wants, in the baseline, never a row here.

_provenance.shape: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on (a) every page statement the vault composes while the core answers every app query, with each shelf, view, sort and filter that changes the statement, and (b) every hand-written SELECT or WITH in crates/{vault,apps/kit,search,ontology}/src that prepares alone, over the year-3 rows vault (centraid_apps_kit::search_corpus::YEAR3_ROWS, about 45,000 entities), closed and reopened so SQLite holds statistics
_provenance.seededFrom: the first run of the sweep (#1135): every finding it made is either an index added to the baseline or an entry here with its reason

entries.reason: kind = 'calendar': one row per calendar the member keeps (a handful), sorted for the page
kind = 'folder': the member's folders (hundreds at most), sorted by id for a 500-row page
the star edges, one per star the member gave (any kind), sorted newest first; bounded by the stars given, not by the vault
kind = 'workout_kind': a few dozen kinds, sorted by id
the Locker trash: a row leaves it at purge_at, so what is sorted is the trash and not the kind
linked transfers only (the partial index txn_by_transfer): two rows per transfer the member recorded, tens a year
the trash: a row leaves it at purge_at, so what is sorted is the trash and not the ledger

entries.statement: SELECT b.hash, b.size, (SELECT variant FROM derivative
entries.reason: the backup pass lists every content item once: O(N) by definition and off the request path

entries.statement: SELECT hash, size FROM blob ORDER BY hash
entries.reason: the backup pass names every blob, in the primary key's order

entries.statement: SELECT id FROM entity ORDER BY n
entries.reason: the index rebuild walks every entity by definition
a pass over every photograph by design: the library's originals

entries.statement: SELECT (SELECT max(n) FROM search_word), (SELECT count(*) FROM search_word)
entries.reason: count(*) walks the word list's pages, 40 microseconds at 150,000 words (words.rs measures it); it is the check that the cache is still the table
